input: A plug-in program by its name beside the application, the contract and version it must speak, and how long an answer may take.
output: The plug-in's answers to requests (JSON lines), or a controlled error when it does not start, speaks another contract, does not answer in time or answers too much; the plug-in program's side of the same contract.
specification: User 2026-10-23: blocks like a DLL so that the application is easier to service. A plug-in is its own program speaking a versioned contract; it is started at its first request and stopped when idle. Nothing falls back to anything.
